title: Persevere vs Pivot Signal Checker
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: Learners switch three validation evidence signals (problem validated, payment signals, customer confirmed) and see whether the pattern supports persevere, a specific pivot, or kill, with a justification and keep or change tags. A worked example uses Priya's evidence, and four practice ventures ask learners to judge each line of evidence, with green or amber feedback on every signal.

educational.topic: Persevere, pivot, and kill decisions from validation evidence
learningObjectives: Given a set of validation evidence signals for a venture scenario, evaluate the pattern and justify whether it supports a persevere decision, a pivot decision, or a kill decision

controls.label: Problem Validated?
controls.purpose: Mark that target customers raised the pain unprompted and ranked it a priority

controls.label: Solution Got Payment Signals?
controls.purpose: Mark that money changed hands for the offer, not just interest

controls.label: Customer Definition Confirmed?
controls.purpose: Mark that the people who felt the pain or paid match the defined target customer

controls.label: Load Priya's Evidence
controls.purpose: Show Priya's evidence as a worked example: signals set, each line annotated, verdict justified

controls.label: Try a Scenario / Check My Reading / Next Scenario / Try Again
controls.purpose: Start the practice scenarios, check the learner's reading of the evidence, advance, or reshuffle

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return to Explore mode with every signal off

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked example followed by scenario-based judgment with per-signal corrective feedback
keyQuestions: Does this line of evidence clear its bar, or is it only interest?
Which element of the concept does the evidence support keeping, and which one should change?
Is there anything left with evidence behind it, or is this a kill?
commonMisconceptions: Likes, comments, and 'I'd buy that' count as payment signals
A pain that only surfaces after a leading question is a validated problem
Any paying customer confirms the customer definition, even if they are not the defined target
A pivot means starting over rather than changing one element
assessmentOpportunities: Read at least 3 of 4 practice scenarios honestly on the first try
Write a one-sentence justification for each verdict before checking
Set the three signals for one's own latest lean test and justify the verdict
